subject: physics
chapter_title: Systems of Particles and Rotational Motion

concepts.title: Centre of Mass of a System of Particles
concepts.definition: The point representing the average position of the mass distribution in a system, weighted by the mass of each individual particle.
concepts.key_idea: Mass-weighted arithmetic mean of particle position coordinates.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: find the centre of mass position for three point masses along an axis
calculate the centre of mass location for a system of three particles
determine the x coordinate of centre of mass given masses and positions
what is the centre of mass of three particles with masses m1, m2, m3 at x1, x2, x3
evaluate the position of the centre of mass for a discrete particle distribution

solution_steps.action: compute total weighted position sum
solution_steps.explain: Multiply each mass by its position coordinate and sum them

solution_steps.action: compute total mass
solution_steps.explain: Add individual particle masses together

solution_steps.action: compute centre of mass x coordinate
solution_steps.explain: Divide weighted position sum by total mass

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving centre of mass of a system of particles.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute total weighted position sum. Step 2: compute total mass. Step 3: compute centre of mass x coordinate. Working: m1 * x1 + m2 * x2 + m3 * x3, m1 + m2 + m3, mx_sum / total_mass.
worked_examples.answer: Centre of Mass of a System of Particles applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply centre of mass of a system of particles to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute total weighted position sum. Step 2: compute total mass. Step 3: compute centre of mass x coordinate. Working: m1 * x1 + m2 * x2 + m3 * x3, m1 + m2 + m3, mx_sum / total_mass.
worked_examples.answer: The method of centre of mass of a system of particles leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Acceleration of Centre of Mass
concepts.definition: The linear acceleration of a system centre of mass is governed solely by the net external force acting on the system.
concepts.key_idea: Centre of mass accelerates as if total mass were concentrated there under net external force.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: calculate the acceleration of the centre of mass for a system
find the centre of mass acceleration given total external force and total mass
determine how fast the centre of mass accelerates under a net external force
what is the acceleration of the centre of mass of a system of particles
evaluate centre of mass acceleration when external force and system mass are known

solution_steps.action: calculate acceleration of centre of mass
solution_steps.explain: Divide net external force by total system mass

solution_steps.action: verify that internal forces cancel out
solution_steps.explain: Internal forces between particles occur in action-reaction pairs and do not affect the motion of the centre of mass.

solution_steps.action: relate centre of mass acceleration to total linear momentum change
solution_steps.explain: The acceleration of the centre of mass equals the time rate of change of total linear momentum divided by total mass.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving acceleration of centre of mass.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate acceleration of centre of mass. Step 2: verify that internal forces cancel out. Step 3: relate centre of mass acceleration to total linear momentum change. Working: f_ext / total_mass, 0, (p_final - p_initial) / (total_mass * delta_t).
worked_examples.answer: Acceleration of Centre of Mass applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply acceleration of centre of mass to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate acceleration of centre of mass. Step 2: verify that internal forces cancel out. Step 3: relate centre of mass acceleration to total linear momentum change. Working: f_ext / total_mass, 0, (p_final - p_initial) / (total_mass * delta_t).
worked_examples.answer: The method of acceleration of centre of mass leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Linear Momentum of a System of Particles
concepts.definition: The cumulative linear momentum of a multi-particle system equals total mass multiplied by the velocity vector of its centre of mass.
concepts.key_idea: Total momentum of a system is equivalent to a single effective particle located at centre of mass.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: calculate the total linear momentum of a system of particles
find the system linear momentum given total mass and velocity of centre of mass
determine the linear momentum of an extended system moving with center of mass velocity
what is the net momentum of a particle system with total mass M and velocity V
evaluate total linear momentum from system mass and centre of mass speed

solution_steps.action: calculate total linear momentum
solution_steps.explain: Multiply total system mass by centre of mass velocity

solution_steps.action: verify momentum conservation for an isolated system
solution_steps.explain: If no net external force acts on the system, total linear momentum remains constant over time.

solution_steps.action: relate total momentum to net external force
solution_steps.explain: The time rate of change of total linear momentum equals the net external force on the system.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving linear momentum of a system of particles.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate total linear momentum. Step 2: verify momentum conservation for an isolated system. Step 3: relate total momentum to net external force. Working: total_mass * v_cm, (mass_i * velocity_i), (p_final - p_initial) / delta_t.
worked_examples.answer: Linear Momentum of a System of Particles applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply linear momentum of a system of particles to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate total linear momentum. Step 2: verify momentum conservation for an isolated system. Step 3: relate total momentum to net external force. Working: total_mass * v_cm, (mass_i * velocity_i), (p_final - p_initial) / delta_t.
worked_examples.answer: The method of linear momentum of a system of particles leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Vector Product and Properties
concepts.definition: A binary vector operation producing a vector normal to the plane of operands with magnitude proportional to the sine of their enclosed angle.
concepts.key_idea: Cross product generates a perpendicular vector and is anti-commutative.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: verify anti-commutativity of vector cross product
explain the right hand rule for vector cross product direction
state the conditions under which vector product of two vectors is zero
how does a cross product behave under spatial reflection
show that self cross product of a vector equals zero vector

solution_steps.action: identify vector components and orientation
solution_steps.explain: Check angle between vectors and plane of orientation

solution_steps.action: apply right hand screw rule
solution_steps.explain: Curl fingers from first vector to second vector to determine directional normal

solution_steps.action: verify anti-commutativity and zero self-cross-product properties
solution_steps.explain: Confirm that a x b equals negative of b x a, and that the cross product of any vector with itself yields the zero vector.

concepts.title: Tangential Velocity in Rigid Body Rotation
concepts.definition: The linear speed of a point in a rotating body proportional to its radial distance from the fixed axis of rotation.
concepts.key_idea: Linear speed increases linearly with radial distance from the rotational axis.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: find the linear speed of a point on a rotating body
calculate tangential velocity given angular velocity and radius
determine the speed of a particle at distance r from the axis of rotation
what is the linear velocity of a point on a wheel rotating with angular speed omega
evaluate linear speed from angular speed and perpendicular distance

solution_steps.action: compute tangential linear speed
solution_steps.explain: Multiply angular velocity by perpendicular distance from axis

solution_steps.action: determine the direction of tangential velocity
solution_steps.explain: The tangential velocity vector is always perpendicular to the radius vector and points along the instantaneous direction of motion.

solution_steps.action: verify consistency with angular speed and radius
solution_steps.explain: All points on a rigid body share the same angular velocity, so linear speed scales linearly with radial distance from the axis.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving tangential velocity in rigid body rotation.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute tangential linear speed. Step 2: determine the direction of tangential velocity. Step 3: verify consistency with angular speed and radius. Working: omega * r, perpendicular_to_r.
worked_examples.answer: Tangential Velocity in Rigid Body Rotation applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply tangential velocity in rigid body rotation to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute tangential linear speed. Step 2: determine the direction of tangential velocity. Step 3: verify consistency with angular speed and radius. Working: omega * r, perpendicular_to_r.
worked_examples.answer: The method of tangential velocity in rigid body rotation leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Torque or Moment of Force
concepts.definition: The turning action produced by a force about a pivot, measured by force magnitude multiplied by perpendicular distance to axis.
concepts.key_idea: Rotational counterpart of force depending on magnitude, direction, and application point.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: calculate the torque produced by a force applied at a perpendicular distance
find the moment of force given applied force and perpendicular arm length
determine the magnitude of torque about an axis of rotation
what is the torque when a force F acts at distance r perpendicular to the lever
evaluate torque acting on a body given force and arm distance

solution_steps.action: calculate torque magnitude
solution_steps.explain: Multiply force by perpendicular lever arm length

solution_steps.action: determine the direction of torque using right hand rule
solution_steps.explain: The torque vector points along the axis of rotation, determined by curling fingers from the lever arm toward the force.

solution_steps.action: verify torque as the cross product of position and force vectors
solution_steps.explain: Torque is the vector cross product of the position vector and the force vector, giving both magnitude and direction.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving torque or moment of force.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate torque magnitude. Step 2: determine the direction of torque using right hand rule. Step 3: verify torque as the cross product of position and force vectors. Working: force * arm_length, r_cross_f.
worked_examples.answer: Torque or Moment of Force applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply torque or moment of force to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate torque magnitude. Step 2: determine the direction of torque using right hand rule. Step 3: verify torque as the cross product of position and force vectors. Working: force * arm_length, r_cross_f.
worked_examples.answer: The method of torque or moment of force leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Angular Momentum of a Particle
concepts.definition: The moment of linear momentum of a particle about a reference origin, equal to cross product of position and linear momentum vectors.
concepts.key_idea: Rotational analogue of linear momentum for orbiting or rotating particles.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: calculate the angular momentum of a particle moving in a circle
find angular momentum given mass, velocity, and perpendicular distance from origin
determine the moment of momentum for a particle about a fixed point
what is the angular momentum of a point mass m moving with speed v at radius r
evaluate angular momentum of a particle in circular motion

solution_steps.action: calculate angular momentum
solution_steps.explain: Multiply mass, linear speed, and perpendicular distance

solution_steps.action: determine the direction of angular momentum vector
solution_steps.explain: The angular momentum vector points perpendicular to the plane containing the position and momentum vectors, found via the right hand rule.

solution_steps.action: verify angular momentum as the cross product of position and momentum
solution_steps.explain: Angular momentum is the vector cross product of the position vector and linear momentum vector, giving magnitude mass times velocity times perpendicular distance.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving angular momentum of a particle.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate angular momentum. Step 2: determine the direction of angular momentum vector. Step 3: verify angular momentum as the cross product of position and momentum. Working: mass * velocity * r_perp, r_cross_p.
worked_examples.answer: Angular Momentum of a Particle applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply angular momentum of a particle to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate angular momentum. Step 2: determine the direction of angular momentum vector. Step 3: verify angular momentum as the cross product of position and momentum. Working: mass * velocity * r_perp, r_cross_p.
worked_examples.answer: The method of angular momentum of a particle leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Principle of Moments for Levers
concepts.definition: For a body in rotational equilibrium, total clockwise moment about a pivot equals total counter-clockwise moment.
concepts.key_idea: Product of load and load arm equals product of effort and effort arm.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: calculate the required effort to lift a load using a lever
find the effort force using the principle of moments
determine effort needed when load, load arm, and effort arm are given
what effort is required to balance a given load on a lever
evaluate effort force for mechanical equilibrium of a pivoted rod

solution_steps.action: calculate required effort force
solution_steps.explain: Multiply load by load arm and divide by effort arm

solution_steps.action: compute the clockwise moment produced by the load
solution_steps.explain: The load moment is the product of the load force and its perpendicular distance from the pivot.

solution_steps.action: verify rotational equilibrium by equating clockwise and counter-clockwise moments
solution_steps.explain: For a lever in equilibrium, the effort moment must equal the load moment, confirming the principle of moments.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving principle of moments for levers.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate required effort force. Step 2: compute the clockwise moment produced by the load. Step 3: verify rotational equilibrium by equating clockwise and counter-clockwise moments. Working: (load * load_arm) / effort_arm, load * load_arm, effort * effort_arm.
worked_examples.answer: Principle of Moments for Levers applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply principle of moments for levers to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate required effort force. Step 2: compute the clockwise moment produced by the load. Step 3: verify rotational equilibrium by equating clockwise and counter-clockwise moments. Working: (load * load_arm) / effort_arm, load * load_arm, effort * effort_arm.
worked_examples.answer: The method of principle of moments for levers leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Moment of Inertia and Radius of Gyration
concepts.definition: The rotational inertia of a body about a given axis, quantified as total mass times the square of radius of gyration.
concepts.key_idea: Measure of resistance of a body to angular acceleration about an axis.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: calculate moment of inertia from mass and radius of gyration
find the moment of inertia of a body given mass M and radius of gyration k
determine rotational inertia using body mass and radius of gyration
what is the moment of inertia when mass and radius of gyration are known
evaluate moment of inertia from radius of gyration and total mass

solution_steps.action: compute moment of inertia
solution_steps.explain: Multiply total mass by square of radius of gyration

solution_steps.action: compute the radius of gyration from the moment of inertia if needed
solution_steps.explain: The radius of gyration is the square root of the ratio of moment of inertia to total mass.

solution_steps.action: verify the moment of inertia using the parallel axis theorem when needed
solution_steps.explain: For an axis parallel to a centroidal axis, the moment of inertia equals the centroidal value plus mass times the square of the offset distance.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving moment of inertia and radius of gyration.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute moment of inertia. Step 2: compute the radius of gyration from the moment of inertia if needed. Step 3: verify the moment of inertia using the parallel axis theorem when needed. Working: mass * (radius_gyration ** 2), sqrt(inertia / mass), inertia_cm + mass * (offset ** 2).
worked_examples.answer: Moment of Inertia and Radius of Gyration applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply moment of inertia and radius of gyration to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute moment of inertia. Step 2: compute the radius of gyration from the moment of inertia if needed. Step 3: verify the moment of inertia using the parallel axis theorem when needed. Working: mass * (radius_gyration ** 2), sqrt(inertia / mass), inertia_cm + mass * (offset ** 2).
worked_examples.answer: The method of moment of inertia and radius of gyration leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Rotational Kinematics with Constant Angular Acceleration
concepts.definition: Equations describing rotational motion under uniform angular acceleration, directly analogous to linear kinematics.
concepts.key_idea: Angular speed changes linearly with time under constant angular acceleration.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: calculate final angular speed under constant angular acceleration
find the angular velocity after time t given initial angular speed and alpha
determine final angular velocity of a wheel accelerating uniformly
what is the angular speed after time t with initial omega0 and constant angular acceleration
evaluate final rotational speed given initial angular speed, acceleration and time

solution_steps.action: compute final angular velocity
solution_steps.explain: Add initial angular velocity to product of angular acceleration and time

solution_steps.action: calculate angular displacement during the acceleration interval
solution_steps.explain: Angular displacement equals initial angular velocity times time plus half the angular acceleration times time squared.

solution_steps.action: verify using the angular velocity-displacement relation
solution_steps.explain: The square of final angular velocity equals the square of initial angular velocity plus twice the product of angular acceleration and angular displacement.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving rotational kinematics with constant angular acceleration.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute final angular velocity. Step 2: calculate angular displacement during the acceleration interval. Step 3: verify using the angular velocity-displacement relation. Working: omega0 + alpha * t, omega0 * t + 0.5 * alpha * (t ** 2), sqrt(omega0 ** 2 + 2 * alpha * theta).
worked_examples.answer: Rotational Kinematics with Constant Angular Acceleration applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply rotational kinematics with constant angular acceleration to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute final angular velocity. Step 2: calculate angular displacement during the acceleration interval. Step 3: verify using the angular velocity-displacement relation. Working: omega0 + alpha * t, omega0 * t + 0.5 * alpha * (t ** 2), sqrt(omega0 ** 2 + 2 * alpha * theta).
worked_examples.answer: The method of rotational kinematics with constant angular acceleration leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Rotational Dynamics and Angular Acceleration
concepts.definition: Net external torque applied to a rigid body produces angular acceleration inversely proportional to its moment of inertia.
concepts.key_idea: Rotational analogue of Newton second law: torque equals moment of inertia times angular acceleration.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: calculate angular acceleration given applied torque and moment of inertia
find angular acceleration of a flywheel subjected to a torque
determine alpha when moment of inertia and net torque are specified
what is the angular acceleration produced by a given torque on a rotating body
evaluate angular acceleration using rotational analogue of Newton second law

solution_steps.action: compute angular acceleration
solution_steps.explain: Divide applied torque by moment of inertia

solution_steps.action: calculate the final angular velocity after the torque acts for a given time
solution_steps.explain: Using rotational kinematics, final angular velocity equals initial angular velocity plus angular acceleration times time.

solution_steps.action: verify the torque-angular momentum relationship
solution_steps.explain: The net torque equals the time rate of change of angular momentum, confirming the rotational analogue of Newton's second law.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving rotational dynamics and angular acceleration.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute angular acceleration. Step 2: calculate the final angular velocity after the torque acts for a given time. Step 3: verify the torque-angular momentum relationship. Working: tau / inertia, omega0 + alpha * t, (l_final - l_initial) / delta_t.
worked_examples.answer: Rotational Dynamics and Angular Acceleration applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply rotational dynamics and angular acceleration to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute angular acceleration. Step 2: calculate the final angular velocity after the torque acts for a given time. Step 3: verify the torque-angular momentum relationship. Working: tau / inertia, omega0 + alpha * t, (l_final - l_initial) / delta_t.
worked_examples.answer: The method of rotational dynamics and angular acceleration leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Rotational Kinetic Energy
concepts.definition: Energy possessed by a rigid body due to rotation about an axis, equal to half moment of inertia times angular speed squared.
concepts.key_idea: Rotational kinetic energy scales with moment of inertia and square of angular speed.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics: calculate rotational kinetic energy of a rotating body
find the kinetic energy of rotation given moment of inertia and angular velocity
determine energy stored in a flywheel rotating at angular speed omega
what is the kinetic energy of a body with moment of inertia I and angular speed omega
evaluate rotational kinetic energy from I and omega

solution_steps.action: compute rotational kinetic energy
solution_steps.explain: Multiply half moment of inertia by square of angular velocity

solution_steps.action: calculate total kinetic energy including translational component if rolling
solution_steps.explain: For a rolling body, total kinetic energy is the sum of translational kinetic energy of the centre of mass and rotational kinetic energy about the centre of mass.

solution_steps.action: verify energy conservation in rolling without slipping
solution_steps.explain: For pure rolling, the velocity of the centre of mass equals the product of angular velocity and radius, linking translational and rotational energies.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving rotational kinetic energy.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute rotational kinetic energy. Step 2: calculate total kinetic energy including translational component if rolling. Step 3: verify energy conservation in rolling without slipping. Working: 0.5 * inertia * (omega ** 2), 0.5 * mass * (v_cm ** 2) + ke_rot, omega * radius.
worked_examples.answer: Rotational Kinetic Energy applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply rotational kinetic energy to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: compute rotational kinetic energy. Step 2: calculate total kinetic energy including translational component if rolling. Step 3: verify energy conservation in rolling without slipping. Working: 0.5 * inertia * (omega ** 2), 0.5 * mass * (v_cm ** 2) + ke_rot, omega * radius.
worked_examples.answer: The method of rotational kinetic energy leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Angular Momentum of a Rigid Body about a Fixed Axis
concepts.definition: For a body spinning around a fixed symmetry line, total angular momentum vector aligns with the rotation axis and equals moment of inertia times angular velocity.
concepts.key_idea: Rotational momentum along a fixed symmetry axis equals moment of inertia multiplied by angular velocity.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics rotational motion find the angular momentum of a body given moment of inertia and angular speed
calculate the magnitude of angular momentum for a body rotating about a fixed axis
what is the angular momentum of a cylinder rotating with known moment of inertia and angular speed
how much angular momentum does a rotating rigid body possess given its rotational inertia and angular velocity
determine the angular momentum of a system rotating about its central symmetry axis

solution_steps.action: multiply moment of inertia by angular speed
solution_steps.explain: Angular momentum along the axis of rotation is the product of moment of inertia and angular velocity.

solution_steps.action: verify the direction of angular momentum along the symmetry axis
solution_steps.explain: For a symmetric body rotating about its symmetry axis, the angular momentum vector is parallel to the angular velocity vector.

solution_steps.action: relate angular momentum to torque using the time derivative
solution_steps.explain: The net external torque equals the rate of change of angular momentum, providing a check on rotational dynamics.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving angular momentum of a rigid body about a fixed axis.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: multiply moment of inertia by angular speed. Step 2: verify the direction of angular momentum along the symmetry axis. Step 3: relate angular momentum to torque using the time derivative. Working: inertia * omega, along_axis, (l_final - l_initial) / delta_t.
worked_examples.answer: Angular Momentum of a Rigid Body about a Fixed Axis applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply angular momentum of a rigid body about a fixed axis to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: multiply moment of inertia by angular speed. Step 2: verify the direction of angular momentum along the symmetry axis. Step 3: relate angular momentum to torque using the time derivative. Working: inertia * omega, along_axis, (l_final - l_initial) / delta_t.
worked_examples.answer: The method of angular momentum of a rigid body about a fixed axis leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Torque and Angular Acceleration
concepts.definition: The resultant torque acting on a body about a stationary axis of rotation equals its moment of inertia about that axis multiplied by angular acceleration.
concepts.key_idea: Net rotational force produces angular acceleration inversely proportional to moment of inertia.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics rotational dynamics find the angular acceleration when a torque is applied to a rotating body
calculate the rotational acceleration produced by a given external torque
what is the angular acceleration of a cylinder pulled by a force creating torque
how much angular acceleration is produced by a given torque on a body with moment of inertia I
determine the angular acceleration of a rotating mass under external torque

solution_steps.action: divide torque by moment of inertia
solution_steps.explain: Angular acceleration is obtained by dividing net torque by moment of inertia.

solution_steps.action: calculate the final angular velocity after the torque acts for a given time
solution_steps.explain: Using rotational kinematics, final angular velocity equals initial angular velocity plus angular acceleration times time.

solution_steps.action: verify the rotational analogue of Newton's second law
solution_steps.explain: The applied torque equals the product of moment of inertia and angular acceleration, confirming the rotational dynamics equation.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving torque and angular acceleration.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: divide torque by moment of inertia. Step 2: calculate the final angular velocity after the torque acts for a given time. Step 3: verify the rotational analogue of Newton's second law. Working: torque / inertia, omega0 + alpha * t, inertia * alpha.
worked_examples.answer: Torque and Angular Acceleration applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply torque and angular acceleration to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: divide torque by moment of inertia. Step 2: calculate the final angular velocity after the torque acts for a given time. Step 3: verify the rotational analogue of Newton's second law. Working: torque / inertia, omega0 + alpha * t, inertia * alpha.
worked_examples.answer: The method of torque and angular acceleration leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Conservation of Angular Momentum
concepts.definition: When the external torque on a body rotating about a fixed axis is zero, its total angular momentum remains constant.
concepts.key_idea: In the absence of external torque, altering moment of inertia causes an inverse change in angular velocity.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics rotational motion find the new angular speed when moment of inertia changes without external torque
calculate the final angular velocity of a rotating turntable after redistributing mass
what is the new angular frequency when a child folds arms on a swivel chair
how much does angular speed change when moment of inertia is reduced in conserved angular momentum
determine the final rotational speed using conservation of angular momentum

solution_steps.action: calculate initial angular momentum
solution_steps.explain: Find initial angular momentum as product of initial moment of inertia and initial angular speed.

solution_steps.action: divide initial angular momentum by final moment of inertia
solution_steps.explain: By conservation of angular momentum, final angular speed is initial angular momentum divided by final moment of inertia.

solution_steps.action: verify conservation by comparing initial and final angular momentum
solution_steps.explain: In the absence of external torque, the final angular momentum must equal the initial angular momentum, confirming conservation.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving conservation of angular momentum.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate initial angular momentum. Step 2: divide initial angular momentum by final moment of inertia. Step 3: verify conservation by comparing initial and final angular momentum. Working: inertia1 * omega1, l_initial / inertia2, inertia2 * omega2.
worked_examples.answer: Conservation of Angular Momentum applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply conservation of angular momentum to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate initial angular momentum. Step 2: divide initial angular momentum by final moment of inertia. Step 3: verify conservation by comparing initial and final angular momentum. Working: inertia1 * omega1, l_initial / inertia2, inertia2 * omega2.
worked_examples.answer: The method of conservation of angular momentum leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Rotational Kinetic Energy
concepts.definition: Energy stored in a body by virtue of its spinning motion around an axis, proportional to moment of inertia and square of angular speed.
concepts.key_idea: Rotational kinetic energy scales with half of moment of inertia times squared angular speed.
question_patterns: in Class 11 rotational energy find the kinetic energy associated with the rotation of a body
calculate the rotational kinetic energy of a solid cylinder rotating about its axis
what is the kinetic energy of rotation for a body with given moment of inertia and angular speed
how much rotational energy is stored in a spinning rotor
determine the rotational kinetic energy given moment of inertia and angular velocity

solution_steps.action: calculate rotational kinetic energy
solution_steps.explain: Rotational kinetic energy is half times moment of inertia times square of angular velocity.

solution_steps.action: compute the change in rotational kinetic energy when angular speed changes
solution_steps.explain: The change in rotational kinetic energy is the difference between final and initial rotational kinetic energies.

solution_steps.action: relate the kinetic energy change to the work done by torque
solution_steps.explain: The work done by the net torque equals the change in rotational kinetic energy, analogous to the work-energy theorem in translation.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving rotational kinetic energy.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate rotational kinetic energy. Step 2: compute the change in rotational kinetic energy when angular speed changes. Step 3: relate the kinetic energy change to the work done by torque. Working: 0.5 * inertia * omega**2, 0.5 * inertia * omega_final**2 - 0.5 * inertia * omega_initial**2, delta_k_rot.
worked_examples.answer: Rotational Kinetic Energy applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply rotational kinetic energy to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate rotational kinetic energy. Step 2: compute the change in rotational kinetic energy when angular speed changes. Step 3: relate the kinetic energy change to the work done by torque. Working: 0.5 * inertia * omega**2, 0.5 * inertia * omega_final**2 - 0.5 * inertia * omega_initial**2, delta_k_rot.
worked_examples.answer: The method of rotational kinetic energy leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Power Transmitted by Torque
concepts.definition: The rate of doing work by a torque maintaining steady angular speed, given by product of torque and angular speed.
concepts.key_idea: Rotational power transmission equals applied torque multiplied by angular velocity.
question_patterns: in Class 11 rotational dynamics find the power required to maintain a rotor at constant angular speed
calculate the rotational power engine needs to transmit given torque and angular velocity
what is the power output of a motor exerting torque at a given angular speed
how much power is needed to keep a body rotating against constant resistive torque
determine power transmitted by an applied torque operating at steady angular speed

concepts.title: Symmetry and Perpendicular Angular Momentum
concepts.definition: For symmetric rigid bodies, particle contributions to angular momentum perpendicular to the rotation axis cancel out in pairs, keeping total vector along the axis.
concepts.key_idea: Axial symmetry guarantees that non-axial components of angular momentum sum to zero.
question_patterns: explain why angular momentum lies along the axis of rotation for symmetric bodies
show that the perpendicular component of angular momentum vanishes for symmetric rigid bodies
verify that angular momentum vector is parallel to angular velocity for symmetric rotators
what condition ensures angular momentum is parallel to the fixed axis of rotation
how does body symmetry affect the direction of angular momentum relative to rotation axis

solution_steps.action: identify symmetry pair of particles
solution_steps.explain: For every particle with velocity v_i at radius vector r_i, there exists an identical diametrically opposite particle with velocity -v_i.

solution_steps.action: sum perpendicular angular momentum components
solution_steps.explain: The cross products OC_i x m_i v_i for diametrically opposite pairs cancel each other out completely.

solution_steps.action: conclude vector direction of angular momentum
solution_steps.explain: Since all perpendicular components sum to zero, the total angular momentum vector reduces to L_z along the fixed z-axis.
